source: Yamaichi Electronics semi-annual report: H1 FY2026 (11-12-2025)

quarterly_data.signal: First half ended September 30, 2025 (semi-annual report): net sales JPY 26,739 million (-3.0% year on year), operating income JPY 6,418 million (-6.1%), ordinary income JPY 6,493 million (+5.4%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 4,651 million (+13.7%). Segments: Test Solution net sales JPY 14,170 million (-17.4%), operating income JPY 4,369 million (-31.5%); Connector Solution net sales JPY 11,750 million (+19.3%), operating income JPY 1,868 million (+254.4%), with first-half sales and operating income at record highs; Optical-related net sales JPY 818 million (+43.0%), operating income JPY 118 million (prior-year operating loss of JPY 40 million). H1 R&D expenses JPY 595 million.

quarterly_data.signal: Management's analysis of the first half (semi-annual report): test sockets for the mainstay smartphones and PCs sold well, but burn-in sockets were weak overall as investment in memory semiconductors and in logic semiconductors, mainly for automotive, was postponed, and a stronger yen versus the prior-year half also weighed. In connectors, telecom products were strong on backbone telecom equipment and rising sales of new products for data centers including AI; industrial products began to recover as European customers' inventory adjustment showed signs of bottoming; automotive products were weak on low global demand and the EV slowdown. The company says it is investing to raise production capacity to strengthen stable semiconductor-socket supply in anticipation of rising global semiconductor demand.
